newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian primary market sluggish in May - Prime.
newsitem.headline: Indian primary market sluggish in May - Prime.

text.p: Indian public issues remained sluggish in May, reflecting a lacklustre capital market that is increasingly hampering industrial growth, a leading database firm said on Sunday.
Prime Database said firms raised 720 million rupees ($20 million) through public issues in May, barely changed from 730 million in April.
The sums raised in April and May were well below 11.32 billion rupees in March, 8.26 billion in February and 16.51 billion in January, mostly by financial institutions, Prime said in a statement.
The number of issues declined to nine in May from 15 in April, 16 in March, 24 in February and 34 in January.
"Compared to even the corresponding period of the poor previous year, the decline in amount mobilisation is 91 percent and by the number of issues, 87 percent," it said.

It said that public issues raised about 116.48 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), out of which 60 percent was debt. Equity mobilisation in 1996/97 fell to 46.71 billion rupees from 88.82 billion in 1995/96.
The statement quoted Prithvi Haldea of Prime as saying "poor resource mobilisation is increasingly affecting the country's industrial growth, specially new projects".
He said industrial production may have grown by seven percent in 1996/97, down from 12 percent the previous year.
The statement said promoters had shelved issue-raising plans, and consequently projects, due to "the continuing depression in the capital market since 1995".
Projects implemented through public issues in 1995/96 fell by more than 63 percent from the previous year to 140.40 billion rupees, and dropped another 51 percent to 69.25 billion in 1996/97.
The state of the secondary market has slowed down the capital-raising plans of listed companies, Prime said. It said only 27 companies went public in 1996/97 compared with 73 in 1995/96.
Funds mobilisation through rights issues fell to 27.24 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 126.30 billion in 1992/93, the statement said.
Haldea said the "investors' loss of faith in both the market as well as promoters has brought the primary market almost to a standstill".

He said "the future also holds little promise, an indication of which is the rapidly declining number of public issue documents being submitted for clearance to the Securities and Exchange Board of India". ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
